text.p: Grain and oilseed exports reported by USDA and private export sources.

CORN SALE - Jordan bought 50,000 tonnes of U.S. Number Three corn in one lot at $141.85 per tonne C and F, for second half December shipment under the GSM 102 programme, traders said. Jordan's Ministry of Supply made the purchase from Geneva-based Romak. Jordan has an annual consumption of yellow corn of 400,000 to 500,000 tonnes.

CORN AND SOYBEAN SALE - Egypt on Wednesday bought 30,000 tonnes of U.S. yellow corn and the same amount of U.S. soybeans for delivery in December, traders said. The official Holding Company for Food Industries bought the corn from Swiss-based firm Romak for $131.95 a tonne and the soybeans for $276.35 a tonne. All prices include cost and freight.

WHEAT TENDER - South Korea's Cheiljedang Corp and Dongah Flour Mills Co Ltd have invited tenders for a total of 21,500 tonnes of U.S. wheat by 0500 GMT on Thursday, traders said. Shipment was set for January 15-February 15 to the southeastern port of Pusan, they said.
WHEAT TENDERS - The CCC will tender Nov 13 for up to 80,000 tonnes U.S. hard red winter wheat, ordinary protein, for Bangladesh. Shipment was for Dec 1-25, 1996.
- The CCC tenders Nov 6 for up to 10,000 tonnes of northern spring wheat for donation to Ghana.
- CCC seeks up to 1,600 tonnes hard red winter wheat for Benin. The wheat was slated for Dec 1-25 shipment.
SOYOIL TENDER - The CCC tenders Nov 6 for 13,000 tonnes of crude degummed soybean oil for donation to Peru. The oil was slated for Dec 14-30 delivery.

BARLEY TENDER - Syria's General Establishment for Cereal Processing and Trade has offered 15,000 tonnes of white feed barley for export. An international call for bids has been issued and November 11 is the final date for offers. Results will be available on November 12. The barley will be ready for shipment in December.

MARKET TALK - Buyer absence depressed German wheat markets where supply pressure from other European origins and overseas also weighed down prices, brokers said on Wednesday. New price lows in Chicago wheat futures in response to good U.S. supply news put additional pressure on world markets.

... Domestic grain and oilseed prices drifted lower in Southeast Asia this week with stocks comfortable and more imports arriving in markets around the region. The harvest in Indonesia, ample stocks in Malaysia and imports in Thailand pressured corn prices.

...Indonesia locked up at least two cargoes of soymeal while the rest of the Southeast Asian grain and oilseeds trade sat on the fence ahead of a crucial USDA crop report next week, dealers said on Wednesday.

Indonesian buyers bought one Panamax-sized shipment of Argentine-origin soymeal for January/February shipment at a price around US$285/290 a tonne C&F and also purchased about 11,000 tonnes of Indian-origin meal for the same shipment period.
